 "path": "continual_arc_notes.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC learned task pattern: broken horizontal bars + vertical rays

## Observed rule (from solved task-c0c557ca)
A grid contains horizontal colored bars with a single-cell zero gap embedded within each bar, plus isolated vertical colored markers near the bottom. Each internal horizontal gap is a ray source: fill that gap's column upward with the color of the horizontal bar, continuing through zeros until the ray meets an already-colored cell in that column or reaches the grid edge. Do not overwrite existing colored cells; different rays meeting in the same column therefore form vertical color sections, with the higher existing color stopping the lower ray. Preserve all original colored cells. Similarly, an isolated vertical colored segment at the bottom remains as-is (in the demo, bottom vertical markers occupied the lower rows; the outputs retained them and did not extend them through the horizontal bar above).

## Reliable application procedure
1. Copy the input grid.
2. Find horizontal rows whose same-color bar has an internal zero separating same-color portions (e.g., color at c-1 and c+1). For each such gap, record that bar's color and column.
3. For each recorded gap, walk upward from its row, filling zero cells in that column with the bar color. Stop immediately before the first pre-existing nonzero cell in that column; never overwrite that cell. Rays are evaluated as upward extensions from lower bars, and higher horizontal rows/rays partition the column by their existing colors.
4. Keep all other cells (including isolated vertical bottom markers) unchanged. Submit exact grid dimensions.

## Confirmed example facts
- Demo 3: row 2 color 7 gap at column 9 gives color 7 in col 9 rows 0–2; row 3 color 8 gap at col 1 gives color 8 rows 0–3; row 5 color 6 gap at col 9 gives color 6 rows 3–5, stopping below the color 7 at row 2; row 8 color 3 gap at col 1 gives color 3 rows 4–8, stopping below the color 8 at row 3; row 11 gaps produce color 9 in col 1 rows 9–11 and color 5 in col 9 rows 6–11, each stopping at the prior filled section. Bottom color-1 vertical markers at columns 1 and 9 remain rows 12–14.
- Solved test: color 2 gap at row 2 col 3 extended upward; color 3 at row 6 col 3 extended upward until the color-2 section; color 5 row 3 col 8 extended upward; color 9 row 8 col 8 extended upward until color 5; color 4 row 11 gaps at cols 3 and 8 extended up until colors 3 and 9 respectively. Bottom markers color 6 (col 3) and color 8 (col 8) remained in rows 12–14.

## Caution
The decisive point is that the gaps are filled by vertical rays, not merely filled in horizontally. Preserve the pre-existing upper-color blocker and do not replace lower sections with one color. In one solved case, omitting/altering the vertical extension along a gap made multiple submissions wrong; follow the per-column ray procedure carefully.
"
}
